newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends little changed, gilt yield rise.
newsitem.headline: India call ends little changed, gilt yield rise.

text.p: Indian call money ended the reporting Friday little changed from the day's opening levels in an inactive market while yields on government securities moved up slightly, dealers said.

Call money ended on quotes of 0.10-0.25 percent against the opening 0.10-0.50 percent, they said. Banks do not normally borrow on reporting days as it increases their reserve requirements for the next fortnight.
Dealers said three-day money was traded at five percent while fourteen-day repos transactions were done at eight percent.
"This is an indication that some market participants expect call money rates to be around eight percent during the next fortnight," a dealer said.
Yields on government securities moved up marginally in moderate trade, dealers said.
"Yields on securities with a two-year maturity moved up by up to five basis points," a dealer said. "Low call rates has triggered off some interest in securities."
Dealers said treasury bills were more in demand than dated securities as market participants remained uncertain over the movement of short-term interest rates.
The 364-day treasury bill maturing on August 29, 1997 was traded at a yield of 12.75 percent, a dealer said.

Dealers said there were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit. Rates on intercorporate deposits remained unchanged in the 17.0-19.0 percent range for top-rated borrowers, they said.
